note: All outlets are fictional. Feed URLs use the reserved .example domain.

outlets.name: The Bayside Ledger
outlets.type: Local daily newspaper (print and web), Corpus Christi
outlets.cadence: 2-5 stories a day; more on major days
outlets.style: AP style; inverted pyramid; 300-450 words; names and ages of residents; attributes every number; cautious on cause and blame until officials confirm.

outlets.name: Harborline 6 News
outlets.cadence: 1-3 a day; heavy breaking coverage during the storm
outlets.style: Short, urgent, 250-320 words; present tense in the lead; practical service details (shelters, closures, hotlines); 'Harborline 6 has learned'.

outlets.name: Coastline Public Radio
outlets.cadence: 1-2 a day; explanatory and follow-up pieces
outlets.style: Explanatory, people-first, 350-450 words; scene-setting opening; data and context; equity and environmental angles.
outlets.audience: Engaged listeners across the Coastal Bend

outlets.name: Gulfwater Maritime Report
outlets.cadence: Several a week; port and shipping focus
outlets.style: Technical and terse, 280-400 words; vessel counts, channel status, Coast Guard port conditions; reports public AIS observations but never speculates on attribution.

outlets.name: Sabal Energy Wire
outlets.cadence: Several a week; daily during port disruptions
outlets.style: Market-wire style, 250-350 words; export volumes, freight, prices, analyst quotes; numbers are scenario values.

outlets.name: Continental Wire Service
outlets.style: National wire, 300-400 words; dateline CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas; broad context for national readers; quotes officials and analysts; overseas crisis never names a country.

outlets.name: Anchor & Rotor Weekly
outlets.type: Military community weekly (NAS Corpus Christi, Army depot, NAS Kingsville)
outlets.cadence: Weekly, plus specials during the storm and after the channel blast
outlets.style: Community-friendly, 280-400 words; families, readiness, base services; relies on public affairs statements; never reports operational security details.

outlets.name: KNCB Coastal Bend Radio
outlets.type: Spanish-language AM radio station (1480 AM), Corpus Christi
outlets.cadence: 1-3 a day; 24-hour emergency format during Rafael
outlets.style: Bilingual (Spanish primary, English secondary); 250-380 words; community-first; practical emergency information; identifies language-access gaps; dateline CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas.
